quarterly_data.quarter: Aehr Test Systems press release: Aehr Receives Follow-On Sonoma Production Orders for Lead (10-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Aehr received approximately $6 million in follow-on production orders from its lead hyperscale customer (not named) for package-level burn-in (PLBI) of the customer's next-generation AI processor for data center training and inference: additional Sonoma high-power package-level test and burn-in systems, fully turnkey burn-in modules (BIMs) and device-specific sockets, and production software enhancements, to be deployed at one of the customer's outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) partners in Taiwan, with deliveries scheduled over the next six months. This is the second AI processor from this customer to use Sonoma for production burn-in; the orders expand the customer's capacity ahead of an expected production ramp of the second device in calendar 2027, and the customer has indicated it expects the second processor to ultimately reach production volumes exceeding those of its first. The first processor is already in high-volume production, with volumes expected to continue ramping significantly as additional Sonoma capacity is deployed over the next several months.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $6 million follow-on orders; deliveries over the next six months; second-device production ramp expected in calendar 2027

quarterly_data.quarter: Aehr Test Systems press release: Aehr Receives Follow-On Sonoma Production Orders for Lead (10-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Aehr says it is engaged in detailed discussions with this hyperscale customer on reliability qualification and production burn-in requirements for future generations of higher-power, larger AI devices, covering both its Sonoma package-level and FOX-XP wafer-level burn-in (WLBI) platforms. The next-generation processor requires independently controlled thermal zones within each package, which Sonoma's multi-zone thermal control addresses. CEO Gayn Erickson: 'As volumes increase, we believe there is potential for significant additional demand for Sonoma systems and device-specific consumables'; WLBI can screen die before assembly while PLBI can stress and screen the completed device, and customers may choose either approach or use both.
